title: Determination of the Amount Presented on a Granite Ridge Pass Account in Arrears
content:
A Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass account that has fallen behind is brought back into good standing by one presentation taken at the desk, and this rule fixes the amount presented.

**The instalments that have fallen due.** The number of instalments that have fallen due is the number of whole months between the day the season opened and the handling date, capped at the number of instalments the schedule holds. The season's opening day and the number of instalments are the figures published for the tier.

**The instalments still to be settled.** The number of instalments still to be settled is the number of refusals standing on the pass account in the three whole months ending on the handling date.

**The scheduled instalment amount.** Each instalment still to be settled is taken at the scheduled instalment amount, which is the financed amount placed on the pass account when the plan was opened divided by the number of instalments the schedule holds, rounded to the cent.

**What is left to the schedule.** Nothing is left to the presentation the schedule will make again.

**The past-due principal.** The past-due principal is the number of instalments still to be settled, less the number left to the presentation the schedule will make again and never below zero, multiplied by the scheduled instalment amount, and that product is rounded to the cent.

**The late fees standing.** The late fees standing on the pass account are those raised in the cycle of the handling date, which is the one whole month ending on that date. None of the late fees standing is taken with the amount presented; they stay on the pass account until the schedule runs its course.

**The fee component.** The fee component is the late fees standing multiplied by the share taken, rounded to the cent.

**The amount presented.** The amount presented is the past-due principal plus the fee component, rounded to the cent; the two components are worked out separately and added once, and no further reduction is given.

### The determination worked through

Hypothetical inputs: a tier whose schedule holds 6 instalments and whose season opened on 20 November; a financed amount of 1200.00 placed on the pass account when the plan was opened; a handling date of 20 February; 2 refusals standing on the pass account in the three whole months ending on that date; 29.00 of late fees raised in the cycle of the handling date.

The whole months between 20 November and 20 February number 3, below the cap of 6, so 3 instalments have fallen due. The refusals standing in the three whole months number 2, so 2 instalments are still to be settled. The scheduled instalment amount is 1200.00 divided by 6, which is 200.00. Nothing is left to the presentation the schedule will make again, so the past-due principal is 2 multiplied by 200.00, which is 400.00. The share taken of the 29.00 standing is none, so the fee component is 0.00. The amount presented is 400.00 plus 0.00, which is 400.00.
